items.title: D'Imperio interviewed by Monk Rowe, 2014
items.q: The first bop record I ever heard was... 'One Bass Hit' by Dizzy Gillespie... I couldn't get them out because I didn’t have enough time to get married... Here I’m playing bass with Charlie Persip who is one of my favorite big band drummers from Dizzy Gillespie’s big band.

ctx.x: What was the first bop record that you heard, or did you hear bop live first. How did it sort of enter?

The first bop record I ever heard was with my father when we went over to Oneonta, New York. In those days they used to have speakers outside of the music store playing the latest things, you know, that kind of thing. And we went in there, and I’ve still got the original 78. It was “One Bass Hit” by Dizzy Gillespie. And on one side was the big band version and on the other side was the small band version. And I’ve still got that 78. And I said, now that got my attention. That did get my attention. And that was…
Did you start leaning towards that kind of music, to play bop or hard hop?
